title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff + regional failover hysteresis
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Background: during a regional outage we observed the SLO enforcer thrashing between local and remote pools which caused cascading load-shedding and elevated error rates. Root cause: a race in the circuit-breaker/backoff state where backoff timers were reset incorrectly when a regional failover completed, combined with imprecise queue accounting for prioritization. This allowed a brief recovery to immediately re-trigger failover, causing oscillation.

This hotfix introduces: 1) stronger hysteresis in the SLO enforcer (retain backoff for a configurable grace window after successful failover), 2) correct queue accounting to ensure in-flight requests are considered when deciding failover vs local retry, 3) a small refactor to the CB state machine to make transitions explicit and race-free, and 4) integration tests + runbook updates.

Checklist:
- [x] Fix circuit-breaker state transitions and backoff retention
- [x] Correct queue accounting used by the enforcer decision logic
- [x] Add integration test that reproduces failover-thrashing scenario
- [x] Add telemetry hooks to measure hysteresis windows and decision outcomes
- [x] Update runbook and alerting thresholds

Impact: reduces failover oscillation and avoids unnecessary load-shedding during short regional blips. This was an urgent hotfix tied to incident INT-2025-11-12 (postmortem pending).

review_conversation: Aisha Rahman: Can you add a short unit test for the transition that used to reset the timer? The race looked like it could still happen if the ACK arrives between the state set and the timer cancel.

Carlos Mendes: Metrics look sensible. I suggest we expose the hysteresis window as a config param with a sane default (15s). Also left a small nits comment on the telemetry label naming.
Jordan Lee: Made hysteresis configurable via enforcer config with default 15s and renamed metric to slo_enforcer.hysteresis_window_seconds (see commit d4f7a8b).
